title: Banyan Soft - OpenAPI onramp & first-call planning
next_steps: Send SOC2 + security whitepaper and KMS integration guide
Provision 30k free credits to Banyan Soft trial account
Schedule 2-hour benchmark/latency run with Owen next Wed
Share quickstart OpenAPI sample and SDK snippet
Follow up on VPC connectivity checklist and contact info for infra team
action_items: Maya: Send security docs and pricing breakdown by 2028-01-19
Owen: Run synthetic latency test plan and prepare benchmark script by 2028-01-24
Sofia: Provide sample request volumes and latency SLOs by 2028-01-20
summary: Intro discovery for Banyan Soft evaluating Redwood for an OpenAPI-backed feature. Customer is leaning toward PLG quickstart to validate time-to-first-token, but has enterprise constraints (SOC2, KMS, VPC) and wants to know tradeoffs between hosted, dedicated, and private. Agreed to credits, security docs, and a benchmark run to validate latency vs cost for targeted model + q8 quantization path.
topics: Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
Latency vs cost tradeoffs, batching and quantization
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Maya at Redwood, with Owen and Priya — Owen handles infra and perf. Can we do quick intros from Banyan?
[00:12] Ravi (Banyan CTO): Sure, Ravi here, CTO. Sofia leads ML, Lina's our sec architect, Marco product. We're looking at adding an OpenAPI endpoint for summarization and agent prompts, want to understand how fast we can get to first call and what security runway looks like.
[00:31] Maya: Great. Our goal today is to understand constraints and propose a quickstart path. Typical flow is PLG self-serve — we give credits, you spin up API keys, hit hosted endpoints to validate. If you need VPC or private later, we have Dedicated and Private offerings.
[00:50] Sofia (Head of ML): Two big things for us: latency under 200ms for short prompts (<128 tokens) and cost predictability. Also, we need to keep early PII out of logs — Lina will explain security.
[01:10] Lina (Security): SOC2 is a must, SSO, SAML, RBAC. We use AWS KMS for key management, want to know if Redwood can integrate or if we need to bring keys. Also data residency — EU region would be preferred for some workloads.
[01:30] Owen (Redwood SE): Yep, totally. We support SOC2, SSO and RBAC. For KMS we have options — hosted with Redwood-managed keys, or integrate customer KMS in Dedicated/Private. EU region is available for hosted; Private gives more residency guarantees. 
[01:50] Marco (Product): On the quickstart piece — how long to get the first token? Like, from signup to test call.
[02:02] Priya (SE): Typical is under an hour for self-serve with our SDK/OpenAPI sample; if you need VPC peering that adds extra infra time. We'll provide a quickstart with SDK, sample OpenAPI spec and curl examples.
[02:18] Ravi: Ok that's promising. We have some internal metrics — 500 rps spikes during peak tests and more like 50 rps steady. How does that map to hosted vs dedicated?
[02:33] Owen: For prototyping on hosted, the burst capacity handles spikes fine up to a point; for predictable 500rps sustained you'd want Dedicated. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput. Also note latency SLOs are easier to guarantee with Dedicated.
[02:51] Sofia: Any advice on model size? We're thinking a 7B distilled model for cost, but might need a 13B for accuracy. How do different model sizes affect latency and cost?
[03:06] Owen: 7B will be cheaper and lower latency; 13B often increases token cost and latency — but with quantization q4/q8 and kernel selection we can often get good latency on 13B too. We can recommend quant profiles based on your workload. We'll propose a model/quantization matrix in the follow-up.
[03:24] Lina: About logs — we can't have raw customer prompts stored more than 30 days and certain PII must be redacted. Does Redwood let us opt out of storing prompts in hosted?
[03:36] Maya: You can opt out of retention on dedicated/private; for hosted there are retention settings and you can also set customer-managed masking and client-side redaction. We'll send the retention policy.
[03:50] Marco: What's the friction to go from hosted to private later? We want to start PLG but not re-architect later.
[04:01] Owen: We design the API to be consistent. The same calls and SDKs work across hosted, dedicated, and private. When you move to Dedicated/Private you can pin model versions and change routing policies without changing client code. Network setup and key management will need work — that's the main lift.
[04:20] Ravi: Are there any competitors we should be aware of that offer cheaper hosted prices?
[04:26] Maya: Some competitors like BigCloudAI advertise lower list prices, but they often lack the production features — autoscaling, KV cache, optimized kernels — that affect real unit economics. Inferra and VaultML are focused on on-prem runtimes and may be a fit if you need air-gapped.
[04:43] Sofia: For the quickstart can we run a smoke test that measures p99 latency and cost per 1k tokens?
[04:51] Owen: Yes — we'll run a small benchmark script. Preferably you give us a representative prompt set and expected concurrency. We can run it on hosted first; if you want a dedicated pilot we can run it there too.
[05:05] Marco: How are rate limits handled? We don't want throttling during short internal demos.
[05:11] Priya: We have token-based rate limits and quotas per API key. For PLG trials we typically raise limits for pilot projects — we'll mention that in the follow-up.
[05:23] Lina: What's the encryption-in-transit and at-rest story? Any HSM?
[05:28] Owen: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest. For KMS integration, with Dedicated/Private you can bring your own KMS/HSM. Hosted has Redwood-managed keys but we can offer customer-managed keys in certain enterprise arrangements.
[05:44] Ravi: Can we restrict model variants by route? E.g., user-facing uses smaller model for cost but internal tools use bigger model.
[05:52] Maya: Absolutely — per-route model selection and fallback policies are standard. You can set routing by cost, latency, or quality. We'll include sample routing configs.
[06:03] Sofia: Any limits on prompt size? We do documents up to 2k tokens in some flows.
[06:09] Owen: Supports long contexts; performance depends on model and kernel path. For 2k tokens we recommend batching and KV cache where applicable — we'll provide guidance.
[06:22] Marco: Let's talk numbers — ballpark hosted costs vs dedicated for 500 rps with 128 token responses.
[06:29] Maya: Ballpark only: hosted per-token pricing varies but for a 7B-ish model maybe $0.01 - $0.03 per 1k tokens depending on tier; dedicated reduces unit cost because of reserved capacity — we'd model it based on your expected throughput. We'll send an estimate spreadsheet.
[06:47] Ravi: Ok. Also, latency target again 200ms p95 for short prompts — is that realistic on hosted?
[06:55] Owen: For very short prompts, we've seen p95 under 200ms with optimized runtime and small model variants, but it’s workload-dependent. We'll validate with benchmarks.
[07:06] Lina: Compliance question — do you expose audit logs for each API key and token usage? We need per-user audit trails.
[07:14] Priya: Audit logs are part of Redwood Console — token-level traces, per-route latency and cost. For Private deployments, you can forward logs to your SIEM.
[07:27] Sofia: Ok we want to try the PLG path. What's included in the free credits? Is it time-limited?
[07:35] Maya: We typically provision time-limited credits with a 30–90 day window depending on the pilot. We'll provision 30k tokens/credits for you to start; you can consume them on hosted.
[07:44] Marco: Any friction with OpenAPI? We want to expose an internal OpenAPI endpoint that our devs can call.
[07:52] Owen: We have an OpenAPI/Swagger spec and SDKs in multiple languages. We'll send a tailored sample with the exact endpoints you need.
[08:01] Ravi: We prefer a low-friction kickoff. Can you walk us through the sequence so we know what to expect?
[08:08] Maya: Sure — 1) Provision trial credits and invite your team to the account. 2) You run smoke tests with SDK/OpenAPI samples. 3) We run a short benchmark with your prompt set. 4) Decide if you move to Dedicated pilot or continue hosted. 5) If Dedicated/private, start infra planning (VPC peering, KMS, audits).
[08:30] Marco: What is the typical ramp time for Dedicated?
[08:34] Owen: From agreement to reserved capacity it's usually 2–6 weeks depending on region and GPU availability. Private on-prem can take longer because of packaging and network configuration.
[08:45] Lina: For PCI/financial workloads we need to prove no plaintext prompts are stored. Is there a hardened mode?
[08:52] Maya: Yes — for enterprise we support no-retention and can run in a mode where logs are not retained. Private deployments are best for strict requirements.
[09:03] Sofia: Any automated suggestions for batching/quantization? We don't want to tune everything manually.
[09:09] Owen: Our Optimize tool suggests batching, cache, and quantization profiles from sample traces. We'll show recommendations after we ingest sample traffic.
[09:21] Marco: Who's required in follow-up calls? I'm guessing Lina for security, Sofia for ML tests, Ravi for sign-off and an infra lead for VPC.
[09:31] Maya: Yep, we'd like an infra contact for VPC, and Owen will lead the benchmark. We'll schedule the 2-hour run.
[09:39] Ravi: Sounds good. One more: how do you handle model updates and rollback if a model regression occurs?
[09:45] Priya: We support version pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic rollback policies based on evals and quality signals. You can attach prompt sets to monitor quality regressions.
[09:58] Marco: Great. Let's do the trial. Can you share the quickstart and security pack after this meeting?
[10:05] Maya: Absolutely — action items: we'll send SOC2 and KMS guide, provision credits, send OpenAPI sample and SDK snippet, schedule benchmark.
[10:16] Owen: For the benchmark we'll need ~30 representative prompts and target concurrency; Sofia can upload those to the shared doc.
[10:25] Sofia: I'll put together a set by Friday, includes short chat prompts and 2k-token doc summarization.
[10:33] Maya: Perfect. Any outstanding concerns we didn't cover?
[10:37] Lina: Just one — data residency: can the hosted EU region be guaranteed to keep logs in EU?
[10:43] Owen: We can guarantee region for compute, but for retention controls and long-term residency Private is best. We'll include residency notes in security doc.
[10:55] Ravi: About billing — can we get an estimate for a 3-month pilot and then monthly predictable pricing for Dedicated?
[11:01] Maya: We'll include a pricing worksheet for both hosted-consumption and Dedicated-reserved run rates.
[11:09] Marco: Any folx on your side who handled similar banks/fintechs?
[11:15] Maya: Yes, we've worked with Tidewell and Veridian — we'll share redacted case notes.
[11:22] Sofia: Quick technical Q: is there an SDK snippet for streaming responses? We rely on partial tokens as they come.
[11:28] Owen: Yes, streaming and socket-based streaming is supported; sample in Python/Node will be in the quickstart repo.
[11:36] Marco: Ok, timeline: credits today, prompts Friday, benchmark next Wed, security review next Tue with Lina?
[11:44] Maya: Sounds good — we'll tentatively schedule Wed benchmark and Tue security review.
[11:51] Lina: I might need a longer session for the security checklist — 60–90 mins.
[11:56] Maya: No problem. We'll set that up.
[12:00] Ravi: One last operational question — how are outages handled? We need an incident communication plan.
[12:07] Priya: We have status pages and SLA-backed response for Dedicated/Private customers. For hosted there's a public status page; enterprise customers get an escalation path and postmortem.
[12:20] Sofia: If we hit an accuracy regression after a model upgrade, what's the rollback time?
[12:25] Owen: Rollbacks are fast — depending on traffic, we can toggle routing to a pinned model within minutes. Canary windows and automatic rollback help limit blast radius.
[12:37] Marco: That covers it for me. Thanks everyone.
[12:41] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up with docs and schedule those sessions.
[12:45] (crosstalk) 
[12:50] [End of recording — total 38 minutes approximate]
